metadata.description: One test and its outcome about one subject, as a Knowledge-family fact any test suite can produce: a CI run of unit tests, a role tested with Molecule, a conformance suite against a cluster, a burn-in against a host, or a generated test against a dependency. It says what the test is, what it is about (a reference to any entity), what kind of test it is, what happened (the result, in an adopted test-report format), and which run produced it (a Job, by reference). Knowledge, not a Resource: it is observed by running the test and curated by a reviewer. Lifecycle is the family's curation reading of the four states (knowledge-family.md §2): a proposed test is an intent record, one under review is a requested record, an accepted test is a realized record with `scope`, a retired one is deprecated with its reason. ADOPT by reference (T5): the result body is CTRF (preferred) or JUnit XML, pointed at and summarized, never restated; the signed projection of a realized record is an in-toto Statement with the test-result/v0.1 predicate whose subject is this record's integrity head. The join runs one way, statement to record. Types narrow the subject and the purpose; a Provider Class carries what only one producer knows.

test_id.description: Stable identifier of the test across edits.

subject_ref.description: What the test is about, as a reference to any entity — a software package, a service, a class record, a host, a cluster.

outcome.description: The test's outcome on the subject, as the report format defines it.

duration_ms.description: Wall time of the test in milliseconds.

format.description: The adopted report format the full result is in.

report_ref.description: Where the full report is: a path relative to the run's artifacts, or a reference.

report_digest.description: Digest of the full report, sha256 with the same prefix the integrity block uses.

job_ref.description: The Job (Process family) that ran the test. Its realized record carries the runner, its versions, and where it ran; none of that is restated here.

file_path.description: Path of the test's source within its suite.

file_digest.description: Digest of the test's source file.

relationships.description: produced_by — the run that executed the test.

adopts.role: the preferred full-result body, pointed at by result.report_ref and summarized in result; the first test-report format adopted here
the accepted full-result body every CI tool emits, pointed at by result.report_ref

adopts.standard_name: in-toto Statement with the test-result/v0.1 predicate
adopts.role: the signed projection of the realized record; its subject digest is this record's integrity head; the statement schema is not restated
the level claims a consumer may derive from the signed projection and the producing Job's own provenance; carried by reference, never asserted on this record

context.purpose: Records the evidence a test provides about a subject — any test, from any suite, in the result format the suite already emits.
context.plain_description: One test, what it was about, and how it went: the subject it exercised, the kind of test, the outcome and duration as a CTRF or JUnit report states them, and the run that produced it. A suite with nothing more to say binds here; a suite that checks a vulnerability binds at TestEvidence.VulnerabilityCheck; a producer with metrics of its own binds at its Provider Class.
use_when: Any test suite's results need to live in the estate as evidence with provenance.
A test result should be citable by other records (a VEX statement, a finding) by uuid.
not_for: The run — that is a Job.
A vulnerability claim — that is VexStatement, which cites this evidence.
works_with: Job — the run that produced the evidence.
TestEvidence.VulnerabilityCheck — the Type for CVE checks.
